title: Keep Rand's rational self-interest defining but only partially mapped
author: Worldview Sorter AI editorial review
currentBehavior: The Objectivism comparison maps construct-NE15 directly to Rand's defining rational-self-interest doctrine. The rule is a generic normative own-good claim and does not establish Rand's account of rational life and value.
proposedBehavior: Keep rational self-interest a defining Objectivist commitment, but mark construct-NE15 as a partial mapping. The changed NE15 rule can neither fill nor decisively reject Rand's complete ethical criterion. Add an explicit discriminator against generic self-priority as a complete Objectivist signal.
rationale: Rand's ethics is life-grounded and embedded in a larger metaphysical and epistemic system. Neither generic moral self-priority nor denying an independent need-based reason independently establishes her specific rational standard.

philosophicalBasis.proposition: The agent's rational long-term self-interest is a moral priority.
nonEntailments: Objectivism from market preference or generic self-interest alone
philosophicalBasis.existingGap: No direct respondent proposition distinguishes Rand's specific rational and life-grounded standard from other moral self-priority theories.
philosophicalBasis.scholarlyDisagreement: SEP describes disagreements over how to interpret Rand's ultimate end and her account of the objective; that internal variation is not resolved by NE15.

sourceClaims.claim: SEP places Rand’s rational self-interest within a broader life-grounded ethics and describes circumstances in which helping others is appropriate; generic self-priority alone does not establish her complete doctrine.

alternatives: Retain direct mapping: rejected because the narrower rule cannot establish Rand's particular rational standard.
Remove the defining doctrine: rejected because rational self-interest remains central to Rand's system.
Promote a new Rand-specific item now: deferred because this release repairs an existing false positive without claiming a complete system assessment.
respondentImpact: NE15 support or opposition appears as partial doctrinal evidence, never a settled Objectivist defining overlap or divergence. Other criteria remain independently assessed and no identity is assigned.
historicalCompatibility: The 1.13.0 catalog retains its old direct mapping for historical replay. The 1.14.0 catalog uses partial and does not rewrite historical results.

approvals.note: Reviewed SEP Rand and Rand's primary ethics essay against generic moral self-priority and benevolence false positives.
Reviewed partial mapping behavior and historical catalog separation; release regressions cover both.

release.migration: No historical result migration. Current comparison uses the new versioned catalog.
